newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1.50 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1.50 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs early Thursday sold mostly steady to $0.50 per cwt higher, instances $1.50 higher, with strength tied to tight hog supplies, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.
Even with only limited demand after packer slaughter cutbacks, packers had to compete for available animals.

Illinois hogs posted the steepest gains, with packers paying $60.00 for hogs delivered to plants, up $1.50 from the top price reported by USDA on Wednesday. Packers also reportedly were willing to pay $1.00 to $2.00 premiums over $60.00 for top quality hogs, dealers said.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold steady, with $56.50 to $57.50 paid in the country and up to $59.50 at plants. Trade was light, with several packer buyers saying they were close to having full hog inventories for Friday.
Indiana hogs sold steady to $0.50 higher, with $57.00 to $57.50 in the country and $59.00 to $59.50 at plants.
Ohio hogs sold steady in extremely light activity at $54.50 to $55.50 in the country and $56.50 to $57.50 at plants.
Saturday slaughter was expected light and no major meat packer planned kills for Memorial Day on Monday.
